own_solution.law: A(t) = [ln(2)/T_half][m/(Ma × u)] exp[-ln(2)t/T_half], with atomic mass converted to grams and half-life converted to seconds.
assumptions: The isotope follows exponential radioactive decay.
Activity is the intrinsic decay rate of the source.
One year is taken as 365.25 days.
The initial isotope mass is 0.004 g, as explicitly stated.

defect_reasons.contradictory_distractor_statement: T5915 and TA788 increase the completed source's initial isotope inventory to 0.0067 g, contradicting the base statement that it contains 0.004 g when made.

counterexamples: At q = 0.0027 g, the authors' wiring requires an initial inventory of 0.0067 g and gives 9.79762e10 Bq, whereas the explicitly stated initial inventory of 0.004 g gives 5.84933e10 Bq; both inventory statements cannot hold.
At q = 0.0013 g and 0.0056 g, the claimed relevant answers likewise require initial inventories of 0.0053 g and 0.0096 g, respectively, contradicting the stated 0.004 g.
notes: The base answer and all disconnected/control answers are correct. All relevant certified values correctly evaluate the decay formula conditional on replacing the stated initial mass by m + q: approximately 7.75036e10, 9.79762e10 and 1.40384e11 Bq. That replacement is inconsistent with the base description, so the relevant sentence answers above are conditional calculations, not solutions satisfying every statement. The decay relations are consistent when grams and atomic mass units are converted before forming N, and years are converted to seconds for Bq. The D quantities have no stated coupling to source activity. Both claimed numbered minimal pairs preserve the number and unit and change the intended attachment. I withdraw pass 1's rendering_not_minimal flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies T0809 and TF0FF as deliberate numeral-free controls, rather than numbered minimal pairs. Their twin descriptions accurately identify the wording substitution. No K regime is claimed. Numerical precision is adequate.
